countybuddy.name: County Buddy
countybuddy.organization: Georgia Institute of Technology, College of Computing
countybuddy.description: County Buddy is a companion dataset built to give geographic and demographic context to socioeconomic analyses. It identifies U.S. counties where the incarcerated, university student, active-military, or Native American population is an outlier -- exceeding 2 standard deviations above the national mean share of total population. The original source also names the specific prisons, universities, military bases, or reservations responsible for each outlier; this ingest keeps only the numeric population counts and percentages, not those institution names. Only outlier counties appear as rows; within a row, any of the four categories that did not meet the threshold is zeroed out. Underlying figures are drawn from several federal sources at different vintages: total population and Native American population from the 2020 Census, incarcerated and university-student population from the Census Bureau's 2020 Group Quarters survey, prison facilities from a 2017 Oak Ridge National Laboratory boundary file (capacity >= 200), universities from a 2019/2020 NCES/IPEDS listing (non-junior, non-profit, 1,000+ students), military bases from a 2023 Department of Transportation dataset, and Native American reservations from a 2021 Department of the Interior dataset. Published by researchers at Georgia Tech's College of Computing (Vu, Baniassad & Andris).
countybuddy.restrictions: Public domain / freely reusable. The source README states the data 'can be used freely'; no formal license is specified.
